tasks.title: Events: recurring-occurrence generation cron (materialize real rows, timezone-accurate)
tasks.summary: A scheduled generator (mirroring the existing guarded setInterval EventStatusScheduler pattern — no new dependency) that, per active recurring template, materializes each upcoming occurrence as its OWN real event row ahead of time on a rolling horizon, so each occurrence carries its own RSVP/attendance (no 'RSVP problem', no bulk pre-creation of X duplicates). Occurrence start times are computed in the template's IANA timezone (default EST/America/New_York) so DST and local wall-clock are correct in every timezone. Idempotent (never double-creates). Honors live template state on each run: recurrenceActive=false stops generation and cadence changes take effect going forward; optionally prunes future not-yet-passed generated occurrences on stop/cadence change.

questions.q: Rolling-horizon policy: generate only the single next occurrence as the prior one passes, or pre-generate a fixed window (e.g. next 60 days)? And on permanent-stop / cadence-change, delete already-generated future occurrences or leave them?

testPlan.desc: an active weekly template materializes exactly the next occurrence(s) within the horizon and never double-creates on repeated ticks (idempotent)
occurrence start instants are correct across a DST boundary for a template in America/New_York (and for a second IANA tz)
setting recurrenceActive=false stops further generation; changing cadence daily→monthly is reflected on the next run
the sweep is fully guarded (a failure is logged and swallowed, never crashes the API) like EventStatusScheduler

regressionRisk.desc: A system-wide background job that CREATES real event rows across every regiment; a bug could spawn duplicate or wrong-timezone occurrences, or fail to stop when a moderator ends a series. Must be idempotent and timezone-correct, and never keep the process alive / block shutdown.

EventRecurrenceScheduler is a new unref'd background timer that materializes rows into the shared events table; a bad sweep could over-generate occurrences. Guarded (logged+swallowed) + bounded (MAX_EMIT) + UNIQUE(recurrence_template_id,starts_at) index + soft-delete dedupe. Pinned by anchor/DST/idempotency/far-past specs.
